profile.name: Angelo Demetroulakos
profile.title: Mechanical Engineering Major
profile.tagline: Robotics • CAD Design • Prototyping • Autonomous Systems
profile.bio: I’m Angelo, a Mechanical Engineering Technology major at City Tech in New York City. I’m passionate about robotics and 3D printing, with a focus on turning ideas into real, working machines through design, prototyping, and programming.

aboutHighlights.title: City Tech — New York City College of Technology
aboutHighlights.body: Mechanical Engineering Technology, 2024–present. Previously attended John Dewey High School in Brooklyn, NY from 2020–2024.

aboutHighlights.title: FIRST Robotics teams FTC 9384 & FRC 333
aboutHighlights.body: Participated in FTC Team 9384 from 2022–2024 and FRC Team 333 from 2021–2024. Captain of Team 9384 during the 2022–2023 season and co-captain during 2023–2024.

aboutHighlights.body: Since middle school, I’ve built and configured multiple 3D printers with different motion systems, designed omnidirectional robots, and grown my CAD, electronics, and programming skills through hands-on projects.

projects.title: Kiwi Swerve Drivetrain
projects.summary: A low-power, affordable three-module omnidirectional drivetrain built for competition and teaching.

sections.heading: First Robot
sections.body: This first prototype established the low-cost, three-module Kiwi swerve concept and provided the foundation for the next version.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The Kiwi swerve drivetrain is a low-power, affordable, and easy-to-maintain omnidirectional drive system for robotics competitions and real-world robotic applications. Using three modules instead of four, continuous-rotation servos with encoder feedback, and general-purpose mechanical components reduces cost and complexity while maintaining smooth, capable motion. A custom electronics stack and Python control system replace expensive hardware solutions and make the platform practical for teaching robotics design and programming.

sections.heading: First Prototype — Build
sections.body: The first prototype uses general-purpose gears and bearings sourced from Amazon and ServoCity, making its pods less expensive and easier to replace. Its structure combines 3D-printed parts, CNC-machined plates, and standard hardware. Each module uses a continuous-rotation servo with an encoder for closed-loop steering; an HTD5 belt connects the servo to the pod. The drive motor uses a longer, lighter HTD2 belt, allowing the motor and steering servo to remain stationary while the pod turns freely.

sections.heading: Electronics
sections.body: A Raspberry Pi anchors the custom electronics stack. Each drive motor is powered by a 10-amp motor driver, steering is managed through a servo HAT, and a 12-bit encoder board provides precise steering-angle feedback for every module. These generic, maintainable components keep the system accessible and easy to modify.

sections.heading: Programming
sections.body: Python software running on the Raspberry Pi implements Kiwi swerve kinematics, translating driver or autonomous commands into coordinated three-module motion. Closed-loop steering continuously compares encoder feedback with the target angle, correcting the continuous-rotation servos in real time for smooth, predictable movement. The software also synchronizes steering and drive motion to keep modules aligned and minimize unnecessary power draw.

sections.heading: Second Robot — V2 in Progress
sections.body: The second Kiwi swerve robot is currently in development. This next version will build on the first prototype’s mechanical design, electronics, and software control system.
